note: Recorded legacy for the ticket-trailer rule over LANDED history (issue #287). Every commit here landed AFTER the shared predicate's enforcement boundary and still does not carry the ticket reference in a trailing trailer block, as measured -- not assumed -- by `scripts/check-pr-contract.sh --landed`. They are RECORDED, not accepted: `governance/isolation/cli.py enforce` reports them on every run. An entry is ADDED only by an explicit, reviewed commit to this file -- never automatically, and never to silence a run. That review IS the control, and it is the only admissible terminal state for post-boundary residue: the commit is already squash-merged onto a protected branch, so its message cannot be corrected (history is never rewritten, GR hard floor), and the gate that caught it has no other way to close. A NEW violation therefore still reds the gate FIRST; recording it is the follow-up decision, not the fix (#836). Nothing is ever dropped from this list silently: an entry whose commit now complies (`quarantine-entry-stale`) or is outside the assessed range (`quarantine-entry-not-assessed`) fails the check, and a missing or malformed baseline fails rather than skipping. The list SHRANK by issue #835 (2026-09-15): the predicate's trailer line now includes GitHub's own bare auto-close keyword (`Closes #<n>`), which is the paragraph the landing path composes (`gh pr merge --squash` over a body ending in a bare `Closes #<n>`), so the 8 entries whose trailing paragraph had that shape now COMPLY -- each re-checked, the shared predicate reporting rc 0 for it -- and were removed. 14 entries became 6. The 6 that remain are the shapes the rule still refuses by design: the reference separated from the trailing block by prose (`commit-ref-outside-the-trailer-block`), or no reference at all (`commit-missing-ticket-trailer`).
